questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The variance of first n natural numbers is:
questions.explanation: For first n natural numbers: mean = (n+1)/2. Sum of squares = n(n+1)(2n+1)/6. Variance = (sum of squares)/n - (mean)² = (n+1)(2n+1)/6 - (n+1)²/4 = (n+1)[(4n+2-3n-3)/12] = (n+1)(n-1)/12 = (n²-1)/12.

questions.question: The mean and standard deviation of a distribution are 15 and 5 respectively. The coefficient of variation is:
questions.explanation: Coefficient of Variation (CV) = (Standard Deviation/Mean) × 100 = (5/15) × 100 = 33.33%.

questions.question: A coin is tossed three times. The number of elements in the sample space is:
questions.explanation: Each toss has 2 outcomes (H or T). For three tosses, total outcomes = 2³ = 8. Sample space = {HHH, HHT, HTH, HTT, THH, THT, TTH, TTT}.

questions.question: Two dice are thrown simultaneously. The probability of getting a sum of 9 is:
questions.explanation: Total outcomes = 36. Favorable for sum 9: (3,6), (4,5), (5,4), (6,3) = 4 outcomes. Probability = 4/36 = 1/9. Both (a) and (c) are correct as 4/36 = 1/9.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: If A and B are mutually exclusive events with P(A) = 0.3 and P(B) = 0.5, then P(A ∪ B) is:
questions.explanation: For mutually exclusive events, P(A ∩ B) = 0. Therefore, P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) = 0.3 + 0.5 = 0.8.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Which of the following represents a pair of exhaustive events when a die is thrown?
options: Getting an even number and getting an odd number
Getting a prime number and getting a composite number
Getting a number less than 4 and getting a number greater than 3
questions.explanation: Exhaustive events cover all possible outcomes. (a) Even {2,4,6} and Odd {1,3,5} cover all 6 outcomes. (c) Less than 4 {1,2,3} and greater than 3 {4,5,6} also cover all outcomes. (b) misses 1 (neither prime nor composite). So both (a) and (c) are correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: If P(A) = 0.4, P(B) = 0.5, and P(A ∩ B) = 0.2, then P(A ∪ B) is:
questions.explanation: Using addition theorem: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A ∩ B) = 0.4 + 0.5 - 0.2 = 0.7.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A bag contains 5 red and 3 blue balls. Two balls are drawn one after another without replacement. The probability that both are red is:
questions.explanation: P(First red) = 5/8. P(Second red | First red) = 4/7. By multiplication theorem: P(Both red) = (5/8) × (4/7) = 20/56 = 5/14.

questions.question: Two events A and B are independent if:
questions.explanation: For independent events: (1) P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B) by definition, (2) P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B)/P(B) = P(A)P(B)/P(B) = P(A), (3) Similarly P(B|A) = P(B). All three conditions are equivalent and true.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A disease affects 1 in 1000 people. A test is 99% accurate (true positive and true negative rates). If a person tests positive, the probability they actually have the disease is approximately:
questions.explanation: P(Disease) = 0.001, P(No disease) = 0.999. P(Test+|Disease) = 0.99, P(Test+|No disease) = 0.01. P(Test+) = 0.001×0.99 + 0.999×0.01 = 0.00099 + 0.00999 = 0.01098. P(Disease|Test+) = (0.99×0.001)/0.01098 ≈ 0.00099/0.01098 ≈ 0.09 = 9%. This is the base rate fallacy - even with accurate tests, rare diseases yield many false positives.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A manufacturer produces two products A and B. Each unit of A requires 3 hours of processing and 1 hour of assembly. Each unit of B requires 2 hours of processing and 2 hours of assembly. Available: 60 hours processing, 40 hours assembly. Profits: Rs. 50 per A, Rs. 60 per B. The objective function is:
questions.explanation: Let x = units of A, y = units of B. Profit to maximize: Z = 50x + 60y. Constraints: 3x + 2y ≤ 60 (processing), x + 2y ≤ 40 (assembly), x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: For the previous problem, which point is NOT a corner point of the feasible region?
questions.explanation: Constraints: 3x+2y≤60, x+2y≤40, x≥0, y≥0. Corner points: (0,0), intersection with axes: (20,0) from 3x=60, (0,20) from x+2y=40 (not 30). Intersection of lines: 3x+2y=60 and x+2y=40 → subtract: 2x=20, x=10, y=15. So corner points are (0,0), (20,0), (10,15), (0,20). (0,30) violates x+2y≤40 (0+60>40), so it's not feasible.
